Warm welcoming first-entry story space, clean and practical rather than luxurious. The room has a simple narrow bed on the left with rumpled ivory cotton blanket; a modest low bookcase with used paperbacks, one charcoal-gray work apron hanging on a peg. A small worn honey-colored wooden table occupies the left foreground: a freshly removed simple old metal door latch beside its few screws and an ordinary screwdriver, a half-cold ceramic cup of tea with NO steam, and one small ivory theater ticket lying flat with no readable lettering. These objects should be visible but proportionate, no giant props. On the RIGHT a wood-framed open window looks down over the SAME style of Chinese white plaster walls and black tiled roofs, green spring trees and a few restrained blossoms of the workshop village, coherent Chinese architecture not European or Japanese shrine. Soft spring daylight through that right window. Keep the upper center of the composition visually quiet with a plain warm off-white wall and softly falling light, useful for first-entry title overlay. Palette: honey wood, muted gray-teal, warm ivory, natural green outside. Subtle rich brush texture, painterly realistic perspective, thoughtful calm literary VN background. assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit THIS existing theater background to produce a narrative scenery variant. Keep the same camera position, 16:9 framing, low shabby wooden stage, small humble community performance setting, warm tungsten stage lights, muted slate-teal curtains, honey wood floor, viewer-facing EIGHT worn audience chairs and their current loose arrangement in foreground, and real tall windows high on the RIGHT showing the same Chinese small-town rooftops and evening sky. Keep the hand-painted literary visual novel gouache/oil background style and overall palette. Make one targeted set change: onstage in the back-center slightly RIGHT, centered around x=55%-58% of image width, add an obviously freestanding fake wooden WINDOW FRAME stage prop (simple handmade empty rectangular frame on modest support feet, not a real hole or window in the wall). BEHIND this fake frame hangs a HAND-PAINTED SEASCAPE CANVAS CLOTH secured from an ordinary horizontal rod by visible short tie strings. The LEFT TWO-THIRDS of that cloth is painted with muted gray-blue sea, a low quiet horizon and shallow pale waves; the RIGHT THIRD MUST visibly remain UNPAINTED IVORY COARSE CLOTH with loose folds/wrinkles and the painting stopping unevenly at the paint-to-cloth boundary. All of this is a flat modest unfinished theater backdrop, not a real outdoor view and not an ocean portal. Show brush strokes, raw weave, sag and rigging so no viewer mistakes the painted sea for a real landscape outside. The painted cloth should be visibly a little larger than the fake window frame and have its unfinished ivory right edge protruding beyond the frame. The original plain door and little cupboard/shoe cabinet can shift a little LEFT to make room, remaining ordinary homemade stage props. Keep scenery low and quiet enough that the upper-central part remains usable behind actor faces; do not fill the upper center with busy rigging or enormous props. Preserve the architectural room and audience seating, no stage expansion, no photographic ocean. No people, no silhouettes, no letters or readable text, no logos, no magic or luminous effects. Keep full scene visible, no crop, target final production frame 1920x1080.
